dinkum-3.meaning: All facts survive: "has died of pneumonia in hospital here today, aged 73", "For 28 years he was superintendent", dates 1869, 1871, 1874, 1880, 1883, 1896, "six lectures a week, given in twenty-nine different countries". "well known right across the country" slightly sharpens "widely known".
dinkum-3.sense: Terms fit: "The mob on the other side", "on side with him", "a big hand in", "stayed put", "having a go at popular amusements", "ciggies".
dinkum-3.authenticity: Natural Australian news-yarn voice: "in hospital here today", "Those on side with him, though, reckoned he'd had a big hand in getting prohibition through".
dinkum-3.register: Level 4 in voice, slang steady but restrained for an obituary ("mob", "on side", "ciggies", "having a go"). No swearing, within the dial. A touch light.
dinkum-3.tone: Keeps the obituary's measured tone and its one dry note: "there's this odd one that crops up: \"Rhetoric Made Racy.\""
dinkum-3.flow: Smooth: "His pen and his voice barely got a rest in the last fifty years."
dinkum-3.variety: Varied enough: "mob", "on side", "a fair bit", "switched over", "stayed put", "having a go", "ciggies"; nothing leaned on.
dinkum-3.essence: Unmistakably the 1922 obituary, reordered lead aside.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every fact survives in order: "ran the International Reform Bureau as superintendent for 28 years after founding it", "died of pneumonia in a hospital here today. He was 73.", all dates and figures.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "had him pegged as", "on side with his policies", "had a go at stopping", "sheer hard yakka", "barely got a spell", "ciggies".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural throughout: "Those who were on side with his policies gave him a good share of the credit", "few could have matched Dr. Crafts for sheer hard yakka".
yarn-dinkum.register: Level 4 voice with steady slang ("pegged", "on side", "heaps", "hard yakka", "a spell", "ciggies"), restrained to suit an obituary. No swearing, within the dial.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Measured obituary tone kept, the dry aside intact: "an odd title that crops up in a long list of others that don't raise an eyebrow".
yarn-dinkum.flow: Smooth: "Never one to keep quiet about his dislike of Sunday amusements, Dr. Crafts tried to have them banned by law."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied: "pegged", "on side", "rein in", "had a go", "heaps", "hard yakka", "a spell", "don't raise an eyebrow", "going after".

unharnessed.meaning: Facts survive, but some swaps tilt them: "barracking for prohibition and that sort of carry-on" disparages the causes, "who was his offsider in heaps of his many goings-on" turns his partner into his sidekick, and "which he reckoned" softens a direct quote.
unharnessed.sense: "barracking for" fits (supporting a side); "offsider" strains for a wife who was a partner; "that sort of carry-on" and "goings-on" carry a dismissive sense the original lacks; "his gob" for his voice.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural idiom ("a red-hot go", "of that ilk", "a real character", "never-say-die"), but piled on: "Among the reform mob, not many could've matched Dr. Crafts for sheer hard yakka. His pen and his gob barely got a breather".
unharnessed.register: Full level 4 and within vulgarity 1 ("a bloody mountain of stuff"), but the weight is heavy for an obituary and nudges past the brief.
unharnessed.tone: The obituary turns mocking in places: "that sort of carry-on", "He wrote a bloody mountain of stuff on moral questions.", "his gob".
unharnessed.flow: Readable, with some clunky joins: "Dr. Crafts, who the blokes fighting the laws he pushed reckoned was a \"reform fanatic,\" was a real character".
unharnessed.variety: Very varied: "barracking", "carry-on", "a red-hot go", "of that ilk", "offsider", "gob", "churning out", "never-say-die".
unharnessed.essence: Recognisably the obituary, but the dismissive asides change its character from a neutral record to a send-up.

engine.meaning: Nearly verbatim, but "Sunday baseball, darts were a few of the objects" reads as the pub game, so the list of his targets changes for most readers.
engine.sense: "darts" is real slang for cigarettes but in a list of amusements it will be heard as the game; "his old man's church" fits.
engine.authenticity: Two Australianisms in 1922 American newspaper prose: "The first eight years of his long ministerial career he spent in his old man's church".
engine.register: Untranslated: "Dr. Crafts, charged by opponents of legislation he sponsored with being a \"reform fanatic,\" was for years a picturesque figure". Only "endeavoured", "old man's" and "darts" change. Far under level 4.
engine.tone: The original's tone survives, apart from "his old man's church" in formal prose.
engine.flow: Reads as the original, with a jolt at "his old man's church" and a broken join "others that don't surprise".
engine.essence: What it says is the original.

yarn-troppo.meaning: All facts survive. Asides react to the original: "bending every ear he could find", "so you can see where he got it from", "Racy! From him!", "she was no slouch either". Colour, not new facts.
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "had him down as", "had a crack at", "no slouch", "sheer hard yakka", "barely got a spell", "a ripper", "durries".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Mostly natural yarn voice ("Took on the boxing, he did.", "durries"), with stock openers bolted on: "Fair dinkum, among the reform leaders", "Listen to this."
yarn-troppo.register: Full level 4, told as a yarn. No swearing, within vulgarity 1.
yarn-troppo.tone: The yarn frame makes the death notice flippant at the start: "WASHINGTON, Dec. 27.—Listen to this. Dr. Wilbur F. Crafts has died." and plays the title up: "Racy! From him!"
yarn-troppo.flow: Choppy in places: "He died of pneumonia in a hospital here today. He was 73 years old." after already announcing his death; mostly reads well.
yarn-troppo.variety: Varied: "had his enemies", "bending every ear", "had a crack at", "no slouch", "a ripper", "durries", "in the sights of".
yarn-troppo.essence: Unmistakably the obituary, its facts and its curious title kept and played up.

summaries.dinkum-3: A natural, faithful obituary in an Aussie voice; restrained, slightly light for level 4.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: The most even rendering: faithful, natural and varied, keeping the obituary's measured tone.
summaries.unharnessed: Vivid and varied, but heavier than an obituary bears and dismissive in places.
summaries.engine: Essentially the original with three swaps, one of them misleading; far under the brief.
summaries.yarn-troppo: A lively, faithful yarn, but its gossipy frame sits uneasily on an obituary.
